messages:
maria: Nimbus Support just DM'd with an incident notice — they found a rotated service-account secret that may have been included in a vendor-side log archive. they say rotation happened at 03:20 UTC but unclear what previous tokens were used for. tagging sec + infra to triage.
jordan: thanks. do we have any direct IAM principals for Nimbus that could access our S3 backups or KMS keys? i thought their integration used a scoped role, but need to confirm.
sam: filing quick inventory check. i’ll list any principals that match `nimbus` or their vendor account id in IAM and S3 ACLs.
devon: running cloudtrail query for KMS decrypt/GenerateDataKey activity from any principal with `nimbus` in ARN in the last 30 days. put query below.
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=Username,AttributeValue=nimbus-integration@example.com --start-time 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z
```
devon: also checking S3 access logs for our backup-bucket: `s3://redwood-backups-prod/` for any PUT/GET by vendor IP ranges.
lena: quick note — our backups are encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh). vendor only had a short-lived service account token for uploads, not direct KMS perms. but we should verify if their token was ever granted kms:Decrypt or kms:GenerateDataKey.
nimbus-support: (from vendor) apologies — we rotated the service account credentials at 03:20 UTC after detecting the secret in an internal log bundle. we do not store plaintext keys long-term. we are sharing MD5s of the rotated secret blobs and have the rotate/revoke timeline. we will provide IP ranges and stacktrace lines where it appeared.
maria: ok vendor says rotated. priority now: (1) confirm whether that principal performed any KMS decrypts or accessed any objects in our backup bucket; (2) rotate any cross-account credentials we have that reference them; (3) collect timeline and classify incident. if there's evidence of read from backup bucket -> escalates to incident response P1 and customer comms.
jordan: sam/devon pls share outputs. if we see any Decrypt events, we must assume potential data exposure and rotate the CMK + re-encrypt backlog or revoke any ciphertext keys. that is heavy — let's confirm first.
sam: IAM check complete: found an IAM role `integration/nimbus-uploader` with STS AssumeRole allowed from `arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/nimbus-worker`. Role policy only allows S3:PutObject to `s3://redwood-backups-prod/*` and kms:GenerateDataKey for that CMK. so suspicious: they did have GenerateDataKey permission.
devon: cloudtrail results: two GenerateDataKey events from principal `arn:aws:sts::999888777666:assumed-role/nimbus-worker/session` on 2026-03-18T02:15:03Z and 2026-03-19T22:41:10Z. both targeted our CMK. no explicit Decrypt events found for the same principal — but GenerateDataKey implies they could get plaintext DEK for encryption of object content.
lena: that means vendor could encrypt uploads (expected). Decrypt not required to upload. but if they ever downloaded and then decrypted, we'd see Decrypt. check S3 GET logs.
sam: S3 access logs: i see several GETs from that principal's IPs on 2026-03-19 22:42 UTC for `s3://redwood-backups-prod/daily/2026-03-19.tar.gz` — 1 successful GET. need to confirm whether object is encrypted with the CMK (yes) and whether the GET returned plaintext (it did). so this is a read of an encrypted backup by the vendor principal.
maria: that changes severity — vendor performed GET and we see GenerateDataKey + successful GET. treat as potential exposure of backup data. notify incident response lead, start containment.
nimbus-support: (vendor) we are reviewing our internal logs to find how the secret landed in the archive and whether any of our worker nodes used that token beyond normal upload windows. we'll share IPs and ask for temporary role revoke.
jordan: containment plan proposal: (A) revoke `integration/nimbus-uploader` assume-role trust immediately; (B) rotate any AWS keys associated with that role; (C) rotate the CMK or create a new CMK and re-encrypt backups; (D) preserve evidence (cloudtrail, S3 objects, vendor logs).
devon: i'll revoke the trust policy now and create an allowlist so vendor can't re-assume until post-authorization. doing: `aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name integration/nimbus-uploader --policy-document '{}'` will block assume for now.
sam: snapshotting the affected S3 objects and creating forensic copies in our locked bucket `s3://redwood-forensics/`. also saving cloudtrail export. tagging evidence with case id INC-2026-0319.
lena: for KMS actions: rotating a CMK is heavyweight. alternative: create a new CMK, re-encrypt sensitive backup objects with new key, and disable the old key (deny GenerateDataKey/Decrypt) for vendor account. that prevents future decrypts without an expensive KMS rewrap of all data. recommend new CMK + rewrap via parallel jobs.
maria: agree. also notify legal/compliance and prepare a short customer comms draft if we confirm sensitive customer data in the backup snapshot. notify product about impacted regions.
nimbus-support: we request a coordinated window for key rotation and a confirmatory list of objects they accessed. we'll assist where possible but cannot access your KMS.
jordan: timeline & next steps: 1) containment actions executed (devon/sam) — revoke trust + evidence snapshot (done); 2) full audit of all GETs by vendor/principal across last 90 days (devon); 3) create new CMK and start re-encrypt job for backup objects; 4) convene incident call with Nimbus and legal at 16:00 UTC. please ack.
devon: containment done — trust revoked at 1773456900. evidence copied. starting full GET audit now; ETA 45m.
sam: backup re-encrypt job queued — will target last 30 days first. ETA initial rewrap for critical objects 6h.
lena: opened ticket with KMS team to create CMK and IAM policies to prevent cross-account GenerateDataKey in future. also adding additional audit logging for key usage notifications.
maria: thanks all. tagging :incident-bot: to generate incident record.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0319 created. severity: P1 (potential customer data exposure). responders: maria, jordan, sam, devon, lena. conference bridge: meet.redwood/INC-2026-0319
maria: final note — we will wait to escalate customer notification until forensics verifies exactly which customer data was in the accessed snapshot. compliance lead notified.
jordan: posting a brief runbook summary to #incidents after the call. :thumbsup:
